sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Scottsdale
sections.html:
Scottsdale itself mails no property tax bill. Maricopa County does the billing: its Assessor sets the value, and its Treasurer mails the bill and takes the payment. Scottsdale adds its own rate to that same county bill, next to the school district, fire and other districts on your parcel.

The city's 2025/26 property tax rate is $0.4891 primary and $0.4233 secondary, $0.9124 combined, per $100 of assessed valuation. The primary share covers everyday city operations, while the secondary share retires debt on voter-approved bonds. Rates for 2026/27 may differ, so read the rate lines on your own bill.

Scottsdale had an estimated 243,006 residents on July 1, 2025. Homes there have a median owner-occupied value of $789,800 for 2020 to 2024, and owners occupy 67.0 percent of the housing. Parcels near the city line can fall under a neighbor such as Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Carefree, Fountain Hills or Tempe, so confirm the city and districts printed on your bill.

The bill is split into halves. October 1 is the first half's due date. Half two arrives March 1, 2027, and becomes late when 5 p.m. on May 1, 2027 passes. Settle the full year by December 31 and half one is interest-free. December 1 is when final delinquent notices are sent.

A bill that totals $100 or less goes late at 5 p.m. on December 31. Overdue tax earns simple interest of 16 percent a year. ARS 42-18053 adds a one-time relief: if the board approves, the treasurer can waive interest and penalties on a delinquency that follows within a year of a mortgage or deed of trust being released. Each property can use it once.

EventDate or rule
First halfDue October 1
Second halfDue March 1; late after 5 p.m. on May 1
Full year without interestPaid by 5 p.m. December 31, for bills over $100

sections.h2: Why a high value doesn't mean a high bill
sections.html:
What the county taxes is the limited property value. Growth in that figure is held to 5 percent a year, with exceptions for new construction, a significant change to the property or a change of use. A big appraisal number therefore doesn't automatically mean a big bill. When a buyer asks about taxes, point to the actual figures on your own bill.

Owners near the McDowell Sonoran Preserve or the Indian Bend Wash Greenbelt should check parcel data for flood and preserve boundaries before listing. Buyers tend to ask about both.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Scottsdale valuation
sections.html:
Home owners file Form 82130R, the Petition for Review of Valuation, with the Maricopa County Assessor. Sixty days from the date of the Notice of Value is the cutoff, and the Assessor sends notices by March 1. Visit 301 W Jefferson St, Phoenix, AZ 85003, or call 602-506-3406. Appeals sent by email are refused. A petition with no documents behind it, such as comparable sales or an appraisal, may be denied.

Two items are open to appeal: full cash value and legal class. The limited property value, which actually sets your tax, is off the table. Expect the Assessor's answer by August 15. Disagree with it and you get 25 days to take the matter to the State Board of Equalization, the body that hears these cases for Maricopa County and issues decisions by mid-October. The final route is court, either tax court or small claims, filed by December 15 of the notice year or inside 60 days of the last administrative ruling. Small claims can hear appeals on owner-occupied homes and on property valued under $2 million. The tax court line is 602-506-8297.

  • A Notice of Claim fits a factual mistake, such as the wrong square footage or year built. It can reach the current year and the three tax years before it, and it may produce a refund.
  • Use the Residential Legal Class Change form if the house recently became your primary residence. A change made between January 1 and July 1 can fix both the current and next tax year.

A new owner of property whose value or class the former owner never appealed may file in court before December 15 of the year the taxes are levied.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
Maricopa County secures unpaid taxes by selling liens, as ARS 42-18101 directs, through an online auction vendor. The lien is a claim for the tax. You still own the house, but the lien has to be paid with interest to clear it. Tax lien staff at the Treasurer take calls at 602-506-8511.

If a lien or open balance is on the parcel, tell the title company before you sign a contract. It will want the payoff included in the closing figures.

Scottsdale charges a 5.0 percent transient lodging tax on stays of 29 days or less, on top of its 1.7 percent privilege tax. Neither is part of the property bill. A house used for guests may also carry a different legal class on the county roll, so ask the Assessor how yours is classified before listing.

sections.h2: Selling a Scottsdale house with taxes owed
sections.html:
• Look up the parcel on the Treasurer's website and write down every balance, earlier years included.
  • Have the Treasurer quote a payoff with interest through the day you close.
  • Ask the Assessor about legal class, exemptions and the mailing address before the sale.
  • Give the payoff figures to the title or escrow company handling your closing.

Exemptions are another thing to check. Under ARS 42-11111, exemptions reach widows, widowers, owners with a total and permanent disability, and disabled former service members. Passing title to the buyer ends the exemption on that house. The Assessor can tell you which ones apply to you. A cash sale changes none of this. The buyer still takes title with the taxes settled, and the payoff comes out of your proceeds. For a smooth closing, gather three things ahead of time: the payoff figures, a note of whether an appeal or Notice of Claim is pending, and the legal class the Assessor has on file for the house.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Scottsdale?
faqs.a: Payment goes to the Maricopa County Treasurer, while the county Assessor sets the value. The city's rate rides along on the county bill, which means a single bill and a single payment.

faqs.q: When is the next Scottsdale property tax due date?
faqs.a: March 1, 2027 is the due date for the second half, and it is delinquent after 5 p.m. on May 1, 2027. A full-year payment by December 31 spares the first half from interest.

faqs.q: What is the Scottsdale city property tax rate?
faqs.a: For 2025/26 the city rate is $0.4891 primary and $0.4233 secondary, $0.9124 combined, per $100 of assessed valuation. Your bill also carries school, fire and county rates, and 2026/27 figures may differ.

faqs.q: What if I missed the 60 day appeal deadline in Scottsdale?
faqs.a: A Notice of Claim can still fix a factual error for the current year and three earlier years. The next appeal window opens when the Assessor mails notices by March 1.

faqs.q: Does a new owner in Scottsdale get a chance to appeal?
faqs.a: In some cases. If the former owner never appealed the value or class, a new owner may file in court before December 15 of the year the taxes are levied. The usual administrative deadline is 60 days after the Notice of Value is mailed.
